### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a1d0b1ee9e428402399f91808923c508c84e0957`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a1d0b1ee9e428402399f91808923c508c84e0957` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f590bbae1201a05d40e4020c85a1e75612a761b8` — the merge of head `843cf4fecd534b83ea05e6f58e1f96aaa0bd525a` into base `a1d0b1ee9e428402399f91808923c508c84e0957`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f590bbae1201a05d40e4020c85a1e75612a761b8 && git checkout f590bbae1201a05d40e4020c85a1e75612a761b8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a1d0b1ee9e428402399f91808923c508c84e0957 843cf4fecd534b83ea05e6f58e1f96aaa0bd525a && git checkout -B drift-repro a1d0b1ee9e428402399f91808923c508c84e0957 && git merge --no-ff 843cf4fecd534b83ea05e6f58e1f96aaa0bd525a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a1d0b1ee9e428402399f91808923c508c84e0957
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a1d0b1ee9e428402399f91808923c508c84e0957` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Cbvcmv8YWFhFJwzjKL

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 新增只读接口 `GET /api/v1/auth/admin/client-address`，平台管理员保存「允许的 IP 范围」之前，就能看到服务器认定的自己的地址（`clientAddress`），以及是否信任代理头（`trustProxy`）。这个地址和保存校验用的是同一个函数算出来的。
- **为什么改：** 原来只有被拒存时才知道服务器认的是哪个地址，控制台也没有正确的办法显示它（#30398，#30313 第 1 项的 server 半边）。
- **风险与回滚：** 只是新增一个接口，平台管理员才能读，`no-store`，不收查询参数；保存校验的判定和提示文案不变。回滚即撤本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address-read.ts`，再看 `allowed-ip-ranges.ts` 的 `judgedClientAddress`。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts -t 30398`。
- **需要您做的：** 无，席位经合并队列落地（非受管面，350 行，非 BREAKING）。
- **席位意见：** ACCEPT。读数和保存校验共用 `judgedClientAddress`，显示的地址就是判定的地址；闸门用 `/admin/*` 惯例 `gateAdmin`，按出厂权限集与能存设置的人群相同，两个边角只影响能否看到自己的地址。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:server#2 · head `843cf4fecd534b83ea05e6f58e1f96aaa0bd525a`

- **形态:** draft, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay `pr_create`), no assignee, no review request; 9 files, +339 −11 against merge base `f273c9fe`; `check-governed-merges --pr 30483`: NOT governed (0 of 9 paths), 350 lines ≤ 3000. Title has no `!`.
- **Review face:** `TIER_DEFAULT` (declaration face: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — a new served route and one server-only ledger row; no `packages/spec` path, no governed path, no narrowing), written here by the seat.
- **Seat read:** `judgedClientAddress` is now the one call both doors make: the save predicate (`allowedIpRangesWritePredicate`, verdict and `COPY` / `copyFor` byte-unchanged) and the new read. It hands `resolveClientAddress` only `FORWARDED_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADERS` plus the transport peer — the same narrowing the settings service applies before the predicate, so the save's input is unchanged. The route is mounted under the auth base path behind `gateAdmin` (401 / held 403 / non-admin 403 before any address is read), answers `{ clientAddress, trustProxy }` with `Cache-Control: no-store`, closed empty query set (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR`), no body read; the ADR-0069 D5 gate runs ahead of it like every other auth route. `WriteTransport` → exported `RequestTransport` is a rename inside the package (not re-exported from `index.ts`).
- **Gate population (dev's open point) — accepted as built.** The read uses the `/admin/*` family's judge (platform admin) instead of re-composing the settings door's `manage_platform_settings` check inside plugin-auth. With the shipped permission sets the populations are identical; the two edges (a custom set holding `manage_platform_settings` without `admin_full_access` loses only the hint, the save still names the address; the legacy `role === 'admin'` fallback reads only its own connection's address) disclose nothing about anyone else. A second copy of the settings door's resolver would cost more than it protects.
- **Deviation accepted:** two dogfood `/admin/` sweeps (`admin-platform-admin-standing`, `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal`) gain a 5-line classification each — they name any new `/admin/` route as unclassified by design; red leg recorded before the classification. Outside the ordered list, outside the forbidden set.
- **Serial:** #30385 (PR #30448) owns the refusal copy in `allowed-ip-ranges.ts` — untouched here; #30312 (PR #30447) owns `applySettings` — untouched here. #30411 also edits `auth-plugin.ts` elsewhere; the later lander merges `main`.
- **Pins:** the real `AuthPlugin` + real `SettingsService` + real routes; each address case reads then saves from the same connection and asserts the read's `clientAddress` equals the refusal's `constraint.clientAddress` (direct, IPv4-mapped, trustProxy leftmost XFF, forged XFF ignored without trustProxy, no peer → `null`); `no-store`; four refusals before any address read. Ablations A1–A9 each red as listed, restored.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial in PR body and changeset; `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-auth`.
- **Dev readings (`843cf4fe`):** plugin-auth 224 files / 3964 passed, typecheck 0, derived gates 68/68 exit 0 (0 NOT-MEASURED), `pnpm lint` 0, full dogfood under the verify lock 419 files / 3492 passed. os-dev-report 6658914828.
- **Follow-up (carrier: seat):** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` › *Saving, clearing and lockout recovery* gains a line on this read once the ui half (#30313 item 1) shows the address.
- **门禁 check-runs:** in progress at ACCEPT; auto-merge waits on the required contexts.
- **落地条款:** Fixes #30398. Ordinary queue landing by this seat: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` on this head.
